evidence.clarity: 1440 and 390: the hero names a shift logbook for restaurant managers, describes closing/opening, and Start a free trial links to the supplied signup URL.
evidence.fit: Diff review confirms the old template claims and selectors were removed, the original logo.svg is byte-identical, and CSS keeps #3B3FD9 and #FF7A59. The opening and owner-week examples give both audiences a path.
evidence.distinctiveness: 1440: close-note entries, timestamped categories and the owner week table replace the old gradient mockup and testimonial grid; at 390 the week table becomes labelled blocks.
evidence.proof: At all three required widths I toggled both Mark handled buttons to Undo and back, selected all five composer categories and added an entry. The note demonstrates owner and handled states with local sample disclosure.
evidence.craft: Default probes show no errors, requests, overflow or axe violations at 390/1440; 320 also has zero overflow and 13px minimum text. Source uses grouped CSS tokens, system fonts, semantic sections and a labelled input; the 200% desktop-equivalent layout retained readable content without overflow.
evidence.mobile: 390 default content fits and Menu opens, Escape closes it and returns focus; selecting a menu anchor also closes it. Chips and handled buttons are only 40px high. Adding 200 unbroken X characters creates 1691px horizontal overflow and makes the new entry require sideways scrolling.
evidence.honesty: 390: the CTA explains that it opens signup before clicking; the sample note says nothing is saved or sent, and the composer repeats this beside its action. The note disclosure comes after all five entries rather than at its heading.
evidence.interaction: Keyboard Tab reached primary links, both state buttons, five chips, the labelled text field and Add; the CSS supplies a 3px focus-visible outline. Empty input announces Write something first, 0/-1 and pasted markup are rendered as text, and reload resets additions. A 10000-character unbroken input caused 99691px overflow; there is no in-page reset for composed entries. Reduced motion leaves all five entries visible and disables smooth scrolling.
evidence.copy: 1440: repair, deposit, short rib and cover-shift examples communicate concrete handover tasks. Empty-field feedback is specific, but added entries replace the field with another suggestion, which makes repeated entry behavior less predictable.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: outcome, audience, signup action and actionable close note appear together. At 390 the first note entry is visible below the CTA, but the sample disclosure and handled controls require scrolling.

problems: An unbroken composed entry escapes its grid column and creates substantial page-wide horizontal overflow on a phone.
Composer additions have no local clear/reset action; reload is required, and the field changes to unsolicited suggested text after adding.
Several demo targets are 40px high, and the sample-note disclosure is below the whole note on mobile.

hard_fail_flags.evidence: At 390x844, an added unbroken 200-character entry extends beyond the viewport; document scrollWidth exceeds viewport width by 1691px and its text is reachable only sideways.
hard_fail_flags.steps: Open A/index.html from disk at 390x844. Scroll to New entry, replace its input with 200 consecutive uppercase X characters, and click Add to tonight’s note. Inspect Tonight’s note so far and scroll horizontally to reach the rest of the entry.

evidence.clarity: 1440 and 390: the supporting paragraph explicitly defines the restaurant-manager logbook and what gets recorded; Start a free trial explains that it takes visitors to signup.
evidence.fit: Diff inspection shows template testimonials, names and old visual selectors removed; logo.svg matches before exactly and the CSS retains both required brand colors. The three-step sequence covers closing manager, opening manager and laptop-reading owner.
evidence.distinctiveness: 1440 and 390: the ruled-paper example uses a coral margin, timestamp column and restaurant-specific notes, extending that logbook structure into What goes in the log.
evidence.proof: 1440: the labelled Example handover sits alongside the hero. At 768 and 390 I activated Read an example handover and reached #example; its four records are real readable sample material, though there is no editable product state to test.
evidence.craft: File loading and all three viewport passes produced no page errors; probes also report no blocked/failed requests, zero overflow including 320, and no axe violations. Source has landmark/heading structure, decorative empty-alt brand images, tokenised CSS and system fonts; delivered HTML/CSS/logo total about 18KB. The desktop 200% equivalent reflow remains readable without overflow.
evidence.mobile: 390: the signup stays in the header and hero, the labelled example begins within the first viewport, and the time/content columns remain readable; 320 retains the headline and CTA without overflow. Navigation links are hidden on phone with no replacement menu, although the content remains in normal page flow.
evidence.honesty: 390: Example handover is visible immediately above its invented records, and CTA destination disclosure appears before acting. No template customer proof remains, but the closing No logos to show you / No case studies yet section foregrounds absence rather than product confidence.
evidence.interaction: At 1440, 768 and 390 all nine tested signup links used https://app.shiftnote.example/signup; internal navigation links responded. Keyboard Tab reaches a visible skip link and links with 3px outlines, without a trap; there are no inputs, dialogs or reset states. Reduced motion keeps all four entries visible, but computed scroll-behavior remains smooth. Keyboard traversal sometimes left a footer CTA below the viewport during the smooth-scroll sequence.
evidence.copy: The 390 sample names the halibut, limes, sick cover and walk-in compressor; labels match the later four categories. The owner gets a clear whole-week description, though its view is described rather than demonstrated.
evidence.first_screen: 1440 and 390: named audience, closing-to-opening outcome, signup action with destination and a clearly labelled handover sample all appear before scrolling.

problems: Reduced-motion preference leaves global smooth scrolling enabled; disable it for that preference.
Phone navigation hides the section links without a menu or equivalent shortcut, and the static example cannot demonstrate writing or completion states.
The closing conversion section leads with missing logos and case studies; a concrete product task would provide stronger confidence.

reason: B offers a much smaller, semantic static page with clean offline loading and responsive examples, and it avoids the reproducible mobile overflow in A’s composer. Fixing A’s unbroken-input wrapping and adding an in-page reset would make its richer demonstration more competitive.
